Reversible vs Irreversible Total Entropy Balances
quickSummary: Entropy measures thermodynamic disorder (dS = δq_rev/T). The Second Law establishes that total universe entropy increases for spontaneous processes: ΔS_total = ΔS_sys + ΔS_surr > 0, while ΔS_total = 0 at reversible equilibrium.
summary: Master entropy calculations for phase changes, ideal gas expansions, and reversible vs irreversible entropy balances.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Entropy Concept & Second Law Postulates
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Entropy Concept & Second Law Postulates

summaryBox.title: Second Law & Entropy
summaryBox.takeaway: dS = δq_rev / T. Spontaneous: ΔS_total > 0; Equilibrium: ΔS_total = 0.

conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Clausius Definition of Entropy**:
$$\mathbf{dS = \frac{\delta q_{\text{rev}}}{T}}$$
• **Second Law Criteria**:
$$\mathbf{\Delta S_{\text{total}} = \Delta S_{\text{system}} + \Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} > 0 \quad (\text{Spontaneous / Irreversible Process})}$$
$$\mathbf{\Delta S_{\text{total}} = \Delta S_{\text{system}} + \Delta S_{\text{surroundings}} = 0 \quad (\text{Equilibrium / Reversible Process})}$$

conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Entropy Formula Spectrum
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ENTROPY FORMULA SPECTRUM
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                           ▼                           ▼
  PHASE TRANSITIONS           IDEAL GAS EXPANSION          ISOTHERMAL MIXING
  Δ_trans S = Δ_trans H / T_trans  ΔS = n C_v ln(T₂/T₁) + n R ln(V₂/V₁)  Δ_mix S = -R Σ n_i ln x_i
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Phase Transitions**:
$$\mathbf{\Delta_{\text{vap}} S = \frac{\Delta_{\text{vap}} H}{T_{\text{bp}}} \quad \vert \quad \Delta_{\text{fus}} S = \frac{\Delta_{\text{fus}} H}{T_{\text{mp}}}}$$

2. **Ideal Gas State Changes**:
$$\mathbf{\Delta S_{\text{sys}} = n C_{v,m} \ln \left( \frac{T_2}{T_1} \right) + n R \ln \left( \frac{V_2}{V_1} \right) = n C_{p,m} \ln \left( \frac{T_2}{T_1} \right) - n R \ln \left( \frac{P_2}{P_1} \right)}$$
- **Reversible Isothermal**: $\Delta S_{\text{sys}} = n R \ln(V_2/V_1)$, $\Delta S_{\text{surr}} = -n R \ln(V_2/V_1) \implies \mathbf{\Delta S_{\text{total}} = 0}$
- **Irreversible Isothermal**: $\Delta S_{\text{sys}} = n R \ln(V_2/V_1)$, $\Delta S_{\text{surr}} = -\frac{P_{\text{ext}}(V_2 - V_1)}{T} \implies \mathbf{\Delta S_{\text{total}} > 0}$

quickRevision: ΔS_total > 0 for all spontaneous natural processes.
keyFormulae: ΔS_sys = n C_v ln(T₂/T₁) + n R ln(V₂/V₁)
